guarantees.claim: When hmac_en_i is low, fifo_rready_o equals sha_rready_i (pass-through).
When hmac_en_i is high, fifo_rready_o is (st_q == StMsg) & sha_rready_i.
When hmac_en_i is low, sha_rvalid_o equals fifo_rvalid_i.
When hmac_en_i is high, sha_rvalid_o equals hmac_sha_rvalid.
When hmac_en_i is low, sha_rdata_o is assigned fifo_rdata_i (bypass).
When hmac_en_i is high, sel_rdata == SelIPad, and digest_size_i == SHA2_256, sha_rdata_o is '{data: i_pad_256[(BlockSizeSHA256-1)-32*pad_index_256-:32], mask: '1}.
When hmac_en_i is high, sel_rdata == SelIPad, and (digest_size_i == SHA2_384 || digest_size_i == SHA2_512), sha_rdata_o is '{data: i_pad_512[(BlockSizeSHA512-1)-32*pad_index_512-:32], mask: '1}.
guarantees.cond: hmac_en_i && sel_rdata == SelIPad && (digest_size_i == SHA2_384 || digest_size_i == SHA2_512)

guarantees.claim: When hmac_en_i is high, sel_rdata == SelOPad, and digest_size_i == SHA2_256, sha_rdata_o is '{data: o_pad_256[(BlockSizeSHA256-1)-32*pad_index_256-:32], mask: '1}.
When hmac_en_i is high, sel_rdata == SelOPad, and (digest_size_i == SHA2_384 || digest_size_i == SHA2_512), sha_rdata_o is '{data: o_pad_512[(BlockSizeSHA512-1)-32*pad_index_512-:32], mask: '1}.
guarantees.cond: hmac_en_i && sel_rdata == SelOPad && (digest_size_i == SHA2_384 || digest_size_i == SHA2_512)

guarantees.claim: When hmac_en_i is high and sel_rdata does not match any of the pad‑specific conditions, sha_rdata_o defaults to fifo_rdata_i (covers SelFifo and any undocumented value).
guarantees.cond: hmac_en_i && sel_rdata not in {SelIPad, SelOPad} matching digest_size_i

assumptions.claim: pad_index_256 must be in the range 0 to 15 inclusive (BlockSizeSHA256/32 - 1) to avoid out‑of‑bounds access of i_pad_256 or o_pad_256.
assumptions.cond: sel_rdata selects a pad and digest_size_i == SHA2_256
assumptions.risk: Out‑of‑range index causes unpredicted read from i_pad_256/o_pad_256, possibly exposing secret key material or producing incorrect HMAC.

assumptions.claim: pad_index_512 must be in the range 0 to 31 inclusive (BlockSizeSHA512/32 - 1) to avoid out‑of‑bounds access of i_pad_512 or o_pad_512.
assumptions.cond: sel_rdata selects a pad and (digest_size_i == SHA2_384 || SHA2_512)
assumptions.risk: Out‑of‑range index causes unpredicted read, potentially leaking secret material or breaking HMAC computation.

assumptions.claim: hmac_sha_rvalid must be driven correctly (matching actual data availability) by the HMAC control logic when hmac_en_i is high.
assumptions.risk: Incorrect sha_rvalid_o could cause the downstream SHA engine to sample invalid data or stall.

assumptions.claim: st_q must equal StMsg only when the HMAC FSM is genuinely in the message‑processing state and ready to accept FIFO data.
assumptions.risk: If st_q is misaligned, fifo_rready_o is deasserted, causing unwanted backpressure that can stall data flow.

assumptions.claim: digest_size_i must be one of the recognized constants (SHA2_256, SHA2_384, SHA2_512) when sel_rdata selects a pad.
assumptions.risk: If an unrecognized digest_size_i is applied, sha_rdata_o falls back to fifo_rdata_i instead of a pad, substituting pad data with FIFO content and potentially leaking key material.

assumptions.claim: sel_rdata must never take the value 2'b11; the design expects this encoding to be impossible.
assumptions.risk: A glitch or control fault causing 2'b11 would silently produce fifo_rdata_i (via default), potentially hiding a serious error.

uncertain_points.claim: If digest_size_i is not SHA2_256, SHA2_384, or SHA2_512 when sel_rdata selects a pad, the RTL falls through to default and outputs fifo_rdata_i instead of a key‑derived pad. It is unclear whether this is an acceptable silent substitution or a security flaw.
uncertain_points.cond: hmac_en_i && (sel_rdata == SelIPad or SelOPad) && digest_size_i ∉ {SHA2_256, SHA2_384, SHA2_512}
uncertain_points.risk: Could expose plaintext FIFO data in place of secret HMAC pad, undermining authentication or leaking sensitive information.

uncertain_points.claim: The documentation states that sel_rdata == 2'b11 cannot occur, but the RTL does not assert an error; it silently outputs fifo_rdata_i. If this illegal value arises due to a fault, it would go undetected.
uncertain_points.risk: A control‑logic fault could cause incorrect HMAC operation without any alert, complicating diagnostics and fault containment.

uncertain_points.claim: pad_index_256 and pad_index_512 are not range‑checked in this logic; if they are driven out of their legal ranges elsewhere, the bit‑slice reads from the pad arrays may access unrelated memory.
uncertain_points.risk: Could read arbitrary state, leaking secrets or causing unpredictable HMAC output.
